problem: The last sentence says 'a bind error explains this exact picture, because the unit can be active while the server never opened the port.' This is wrong. If nginx cannot bind its port it exits, and systemd marks the unit failed, not active (running). The active-but-unreachable picture has other causes: the server listens on a different port or address, or a firewall drops the packets.
fix: Replace with: 'Read journalctl -u nginx as well. The unit can be active while the server listens on a different port or address than the one you tested (for example Listen 8080 in nginx.conf), or while a firewall drops the packet. A bind failure would make the unit failed, not active.'

problem: The list 'enabled, disabled or static' is incomplete. is-enabled can also print masked, masked-runtime, indirect, generated, transient and alias. A student who sees 'masked' in the lab will think the command is broken.
fix: Say: prints enabled, disabled or static, and can also print masked (unit blocked from starting at all) or indirect/generated in special cases.

problem: 'If the unit has no ExecReload, reload does nothing useful' is not accurate. systemctl reload fails outright with 'Job type reload is not applicable for unit nginx.service' and returns a non-zero exit code, so the command visibly refuses rather than silently doing nothing.
fix: Say: if the unit file has no ExecReload, systemctl reload refuses the job with an error instead of re-reading anything.

problem: is-active can also print activating, deactivating and reloading, not only active, inactive or failed. A slow-starting service shows activating and a script that tests only for 'failed' would misread it.
fix: Say: usually prints active, inactive or failed, and can briefly print activating or deactivating while a job is in progress.

problem: ss -ltnp shows the process name and PID in the -p column only for processes owned by the user running it. Run without sudo, the nginx line shows no process, which confuses students checking their own answer.
fix: Use sudo ss -ltnp | grep :80 so the -p column shows the nginx process.

problem: The link is not always created under multi-user.target.wants. The directory comes from the WantedBy= line in the unit's [Install] section, so a unit with WantedBy=graphical.target or WantedBy=timers.target lands elsewhere.
fix: Say: add or remove a symbolic link in the .wants directory of the target named in the unit's [Install] section, for nginx /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/.
